{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Form of Transfer and Servicing Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Issuer / Depositor)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Form of Transfer and Servicing Agreement (Cellco as Servicer, Custodian and Marketing Agent)

---

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. Of 19 rules assessed, **12 sit at or above the preferred or fallback position and need no redline**, **5 are deviations** requiring a proposed edit, and **1 (termination for convenience) requires further internal review** because our proposed cure did not verify.

The overall risk posture is favourable to us on the classic commercial-terms axis. There is **no liability cap of any kind** in the document, so the counterparty's exposure in amount is unlimited while our entities enjoy the benefit of the Section 9.6 limited-recourse and Section 9.7 provisions; we are deliberately not introducing a cap that would only weaken our position. Likewise there is **no exclusivity, no non-compete, no MFN, no minimum-volume commitment, no non-solicit, no auto-renewal, no Customer-payable liquidated damages, and no audit right running against us** — every review right in the document runs in our favour. Governing law and venue are New York, which we accept.

The deviations cluster in the **intellectual property, licensing, transition and warranty** areas, which this financing-form document simply does not address:

- **No licence grant at all** — Section 7.5(b) affirmatively disclaims any obligation on the Servicer to license its servicing software, leaving us with nothing transferable on a merger or acquisition. This is the walk-away outcome under the licence rule.
- **No insurance covenant at all**, notwithstanding that Cellco handles Obligor account and payment information. Also walk-away territory.
- **No IP/deliverables/data licence**, leaving us with no rights in the Receivable Files, Monthly Investor Reports and records generated for us and held on Cellco's systems, and no limit on the Servicer's use of our data.
- **Vendor indemnity excludes third-party IP infringement**, with no procure/modify/replace/refund remedies.
- **Assignment** is not subject to a reasonableness standard, omits Issuer/Depositor consent, and the Section 7.6(d) carve-out permits outright assignment to any Cellco Affiliate with no consent from us.
- **Transition assistance** has no minimum period and no outside delivery date.
- **Performance warranty** for systems and reports is absent, with no warranty duration or repair/replace/refund remedy.

Our proposed edits are targeted and additive: in each case we take the **fallback** level, not the preferred position, and we leave the counterparty's existing carve-outs intact wherever possible.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Compliant | § VI Servicer and Marketing Agent | No cap anywhere; counterparty exposure unlimited. Sits above fallback and benefits us — no redline. |
| 2 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § X Miscellaneous | § 10.2(a) omits Issuer/Depositor consent and any reasonableness standard; § 7.6(d) permits consent-free Affiliate assignment. |
| 3 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § III Servicing of Receivables | Bare appointments only; Successor Servicer regime confirms no lock-in. |
| 4 | High | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | § VI Servicer and Marketing Agent | § 6.3 indemnity exists but carries no third-party IP infringement cover or associated remedies. |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § III Servicing of Receivables | No LDs, penalties or early-termination fee payable by us. |
| 6 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination; Successor Servicer | No licence grant; § 7.5(b) disclaims any licensing obligation. Walk-away outcome as drafted. |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § V Depositor | No restrictive covenant binds our entities. |
| 8 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Needs review** | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination; Successor Servicer | No Customer convenience exit; term runs to final payment. Proposed § 7.7 cure did not verify — see Next steps. |
| 9 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § III Servicing of Receivables | No audit right runs against us; §§ 3.6, 3.4(e), 6.6/6.7 and Art. XI all run in our favour. |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § X Miscellaneous | § 10.5 New York (entrenched); § 10.6 SDNY / NY State courts. Nonexclusive rather than exclusive — noted, not redlined. |
| 11 | Medium | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § X Miscellaneous | No insurance covenant of any kind. Walk-away territory given data handling. |
| 12 | Medium | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Missing** | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination; Successor Servicer | Only IP-adjacent term (§ 7.5(b)) runs one way; no licence to deliverables, no limit on Servicer use of our data. |
| 13 | Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § III Servicing of Receivables | No MFN or right-to-match; fixed Servicing Fee construct. |
| 14 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § II Transfer and Acquisition | Payment only for Receivables actually acquired; § 2.1(c) confirms no other Issuer obligations. |
| 15 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § VI Servicer and Marketing Agent | No solicitation, no-poach or no-hire covenant on us. |
| 16 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | § VIII Termination | No renewal mechanic; term runs to final payment under § 8.3; extension only by written amendment under § 10.4. |
| 17 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | **Deviation** | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination; Successor Servicer | § 7.5 mechanic exists but no minimum assistance period and only an "as soon as practicable" delivery standard. |
| 18 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § III Servicing of Receivables | Performance standard only (§ 3.2(a)); no conformance warranty, duration or repair/replace/refund remedy. |

---

## Walk-away items

Two findings sit in walk-away territory as currently drafted. Neither is a reason to walk from the transaction if cured at the fallback level, but both should be treated as must-fix before signature:

1. **No licence rights whatsoever (LICENSE, § 7.5(b)).** Section 7.5(b) expressly disclaims any obligation on the Servicer to provide, license or assign its servicing software or applications. That leaves us with no licensed rights, no route to extend rights to our Affiliates, and nothing transferable on a merger or acquisition — the walk-away outcome under the playbook.
2. **No insurance covenant (INSURANCE).** The Agreement contains no Servicer coverage obligation; the only insurance references are Obligor premiums and FDIC deposit insurance in the "Qualified Institution" definition. Given that Cellco services the Receivables and handles Obligor account and payment information, the absence of coverage sits in walk-away territory.

We note for completeness that the GOVLAW and IP findings were each tested against their walk-away triggers and cleared: the Article XI JAMS/AAA mechanic is optional, narrow and seated in New York (not a mandatory foreign arbitration), and nothing in the Agreement purports to assign our IP or data to Cellco.

---

## Next steps

1. **Resolve the T4C item internally before it goes to the counterparty.** Our proposed new Section 7.7 (30-day Issuer convenience termination with pro rata refund of prepaid fees, plus conforming relettering of Section 8.3) did not pass verification. We should decide whether an unconditional convenience exit is workable in a self-liquidating securitization structure — and, if not, document the commercial rationale for accepting the position — rather than sending an unverified edit.
2. **Issue the five verified redlines** as a single mark-up, each at the fallback level:
   - **ASSIGN** — require Issuer consent (not unreasonably withheld) for any Servicer assignment, including the § 7.6(d) Affiliate route, and bar assignment to a competitor. Section 5.3 (our successor rights) left untouched.
   - **INDEMN** — new § 6.3(e) Servicer IP infringement indemnity with customary exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3x annual Servicing Fee super-cap drafted so it applies only to the new indemnity and does not cut back our uncapped § 6.3(a) rights.
   - **LICENSE** — a single sentence after § 7.5(b) licensing the Servicer's processes, models and servicing software to the Issuer and Depositor as necessary to service or have serviced the Receivables, extendable to Affiliates on written notice and transferable to an M&A successor, with the existing Successor Servicer / third-party carve-out retained verbatim. Note that this override operates on the § 7.5(b) sentence.
   - **TRANSITION** — 90-day transition assistance period and 30-day outside date for delivery of the Receivable Files and records.
   - **WARRANTY** — fallback performance warranty (90 days software conformance to documentation, 30 days services) with repair/replacement or refund, drafted as a specific Servicer obligation for § 6.2(a) purposes and outside the narrow § 3.3(g) sole-remedy language.
3. **Insert the two gap-fillers** for the missing rules: new § 10.14 insurance covenant (E&O USD 1,000,000; cyber/privacy USD 2,000,000) and the fallback deliverables/data licence with a limit on the Servicer's processing of Issuer data.
4. **Hold the line on the no-cap position.** We should not table, and should resist, any counterparty request to introduce an aggregate liability cap or a general mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential damages; the current silence leaves the Servicer's exposure unlimited and is better than our fallback.
5. **Confirm no drafting drift** on the compliant items — in particular that any counterparty turn does not introduce exclusivity, MFN, minimum-volume, non-solicit, renewal or Customer-side audit language, none of which appears today.

*[Playbook] References in this memo are to sections and page markers identified in the verified findings only; we have not extrapolated beyond them.*"}
